ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The solar cell I-V characteristic curve in the figure takes current I as the vertical axis and voltage V as the horizontal axis; the curve marks I_SC = 180 mA at the short-circuit point and marks V_OC = 0.5 V at the open-circuit point. Reasoning: The incident light power density is 100 mW/cm^2, and the cell area is 3 cm^2, so the total incident power P_in = 100 × 3 = 300 mW. The fill factor FF = 0.7, therefore the maximum output power P_max = FF × V_OC × I_SC = 0.7 × 0.5 V × 180 mA = 63 mW. Efficiency = P_max / P_in × 100% = 63 / 300 × 100% = 21%.

Use the given fill factor 0.7 to get maximum electrical output P_max = 0.7 × 0.5 V × 180 mA = 63 mW. Then efficiency = 63/300 × 100 = 21%.
